memories.author: D03
memories.text: PRESENTING COMPLAINT: 85‑year‑old man reviews atrial fibrillation, rheumatoid arthritis and COPD. EXAMINATION: BP 138/82 mmHg, weight 68 kg, BMI 22.8 (normal). Pulse irregularly irregular 92 bpm. Lungs clear, mild wheeze at bases. Joints: mild swelling of MCP joints, no deformity. IMPRESSION: Stable AF on apixaban and bisoprolol, RA on methotrexate/hydroxychloroquine/low‑dose prednisolone, COPD on tiotropium and salbutamol PRN. ARRANGEMENTS: Continue current meds. Order baseline labs: INR, creatinine, TSH, lipid profile, fasting glucose, ESR, CRP, RF, anti‑CCP, LFT. ECG today. Return if: chest pain, breathlessness > usual, fever >39°C, sudden leg swelling, bleeding, worsening joint pain.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Apixaban 5 mg twice daily
Bisoprolol 2.5 mg once daily
Warfarin 3 mg once daily (INR target 2‑3)
Methotrexate 10 mg once weekly
Folic acid 5 mg once weekly
Hydroxychloroquine 200 mg once daily
Prednisolone 5 mg once daily
Tiotropium inhaler 2 puffs once daily
Salbutamol inhaler 2 puffs as needed
Budesonide‑formoterol 200/6 inhaler 2 puffs twice daily

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
INR 2.4 (target 2‑3)
Serum creatinine 102 µmol/L (eGFR 62 mL/min/1.73m2)
TSH 2.1 mIU/L (0.27‑4.2)
Lipid profile: Total cholesterol 4.8 mmol/L (<5.2), LDL 2.9 (<2.6 borderline), HDL 1.2 (>1.0), Triglycerides 1.4 (<1.7)
Fasting blood sugar 5.6 mmol/L (3.9‑5.5) – slightly elevated
ESR 18 mm/hr (0‑20)
CRP 4 mg/L (<5)
Rheumatoid factor 12 IU/ml (<14) – negative
Anti‑CCP 5 U/ml (<20) – negative
Liver function: ALT 22 U/L (<40), AST 20 U/L (<38), ALP 78 U/L (<120), GGT 30 U/L (<50), Bilirubin 9 µmol/L (<21)

memories.author: D03
memories.text: 12‑lead ECG: Irregularly irregular rhythm with absent P waves, ventricular rate 94 bpm. No ST‑segment changes. Consistent with atrial fibrillation, controlled rate.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Mild increase in joint stiffness, occasional dyspnoea on exertion. EXAMINATION: BP 140/84 mmHg, weight 68.5 kg, BMI 23.1 (overweight). Advised on diet and activity. Pulse irregular 88 bpm. Lungs: mild bilateral wheeze, SpO2 94% on room air. Joints: tender MCP and PIP joints, no effusion. IMPRESSION: AF stable, RA mild flare, COPD stable. ARRANGEMENTS: Continue meds, consider short‑course prednisolone if joint pain worsens. Review INR in 2 weeks. Return if: chest pain, severe breathlessness, fever >39°C, bleeding, joint swelling with redness, sudden drop in SpO2 <90%.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Warfarin dose increased to 4 mg once daily (INR target 2‑3)
All other medications unchanged.

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
INR 2.8 (target 2‑3)
Serum creatinine 99 µmol/L (eGFR 65)
TSH 2.0 mIU/L
Lipid profile: Total cholesterol 4.6, LDL 2.7, HDL 1.3, Triglycerides 1.3
Fasting blood sugar 5.5 mmol/L (upper limit normal)
ESR 16 mm/hr
CRP 3 mg/L

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Spirometry: FEV1 1.68 L (55% predicted), FVC 2.30 L (70% predicted), FEV1/FVC 0.73 (below 0.70 threshold – indicates obstruction). Chest X‑ray: Hyperinflated lungs, flattened diaphragms, no acute infiltrate. Consistent with moderate COPD.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Routine follow‑up. EXAMINATION: BP 138/80 mmHg, weight 68 kg, BMI 22.8 (normal). Pulse irregular 90 bpm. Lungs clear, SpO2 96%. Joints: minimal tenderness, no swelling. IMPRESSION: AF adequately rate‑controlled, RA in remission, COPD stable. ARRANGEMENTS: Continue current meds. Offer influenza vaccine (date to be arranged). Return if: chest pain, breathlessness > usual, fever >39°C, bleeding, worsening joint pain, sudden drop in SpO2.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Tiotropium inhaler 2 puffs once daily (continued)
Salbutamol inhaler as needed
Budesonide‑formoterol 200/6 inhaler 2 puffs twice daily (continued)
All other meds unchanged.

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
INR 2.6 (target 2‑3)
Serum creatinine 101 µmol/L (eGFR 61)
TSH 2.2 mIU/L
Lipid profile: Total cholesterol 4.7, LDL 2.8, HDL 1.2, Triglycerides 1.5
Fasting blood sugar 5.6 mmol/L (slightly above)
ESR 17 mm/hr
CRP 4 mg/L

memories.author: patient
memories.text: Via clinic app: ‘Over the past week I have felt more short of breath when walking to the mailbox and need to use my salbutamol inhaler more often. My joints also feel a bit stiff in the mornings.’

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Referral to Dr S. Kumar, Pulmonology, Vydehi Hospital. Reason: Evaluation of worsening COPD symptoms and need for possible step‑up therapy. Include recent spirometry, chest X‑ray, and medication list.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Pulmonology review: Patient demonstrates moderate COPD with reversible component. Recommended to add long‑acting muscarinic antagonist (already on tiotropium) and consider inhaled corticosteroid‑LABA combination (already on budesonide‑formoterol). Advised to continue current inhalers, ensure proper technique, and schedule follow‑up in 3 months. No change in medication required at this time.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Post‑pulmonology review, mild increase in morning joint stiffness. EXAMINATION: BP 140/82 mmHg, weight 68.2 kg, BMI 22.9 (overweight). Advised on diet and activity. Pulse irregular 92 bpm. Lungs: mild wheeze at bases, SpO2 95%. Joints: tender MCP joints, no swelling. IMPRESSION: AF stable, RA mild symptomatic flare, COPD stable per pulmonology advice. ARRANGEMENTS: Continue meds, consider short tapering prednisolone 5 mg OD for 5 days if joint pain worsens. Review INR in 2 weeks. Return if: chest pain, breathlessness > usual, fever >39°C, bleeding, worsening joint pain with redness, sudden SpO2 drop <90%.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Prednisolone dose increased to 7.5 mg once daily for 5 days, then taper to 5 mg once daily
All other medications unchanged.

ESR 15 mm/hr

Liver function: ALT 24 U/L, AST 21 U/L, ALP 80 U/L, GGT 32 U/L, Bilirubin 10 µmol/L (all within normal limits)

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Appointment booked for 2026-05-15 at 10:30 am with Dr Priya Natarajan (D03) for routine follow‑up. Patient reminded to bring medication list and to wear loose clothing for spirometry if needed.
